author: Arvind Narayanan & Sayash Kapoor
title: AI as Normal Technology
central_scenario_summary: AI is a transformative general-purpose technology, but a 'normal' one like electricity or the internet: its economic and societal impacts arrive slowly, over decades, because application development and diffusion—not methods progress—are the binding constraints, especially in consequential and safety-critical domains. Superintelligence and fast-takeoff scenarios are rejected as incoherent; humans and organizations remain in control, with a growing share of human work consisting of AI control, specification, and oversight. The risks that matter most are systemic and political—inequality, concentration of power, labor-market disruption—arising from people and firms using AI within capitalism, and the right policy posture is resilience, competition, and preventing concentration rather than nonproliferation.

quotes.text: To view AI as normal is not to understate its impact—even transformative, general-purpose technologies such as electricity and the internet are "normal" in our conception.

inequality_prediction.score: If AI is normal technology, its downsides will mirror those of previous technologies deployed in capitalistic societies: increasing inequality, job losses in specific occupations, worsening labor conditions, and concentration of power—driven by people and firms using AI for their own ends, not by rogue AI. These systemic risks are the ones policy should prioritize, via resilience, competition, and equitable labor markets.
